summary_paragraph: A 2-month postpartum patient with a history of endometriosis, bipolar disorder, and substance use disorder was admitted for persistent left lower quadrant abdominal pain and tachycardia. The pain began after restarting oral contraceptives and was consistent with prior endometriosis flares. Imaging studies, including pelvic ultrasound and CT scan, showed no acute pathology. Pain was managed with NSAIDs, acetaminophen, tramadol, lidocaine patches, and PRN IV morphine, with gradual improvement. Tachycardia, initially at 130, resolved with IV fluids and pain control, attributed to hypovolemia and pain. A single episode of self-limited rectal bleeding was noted but not concerning. The patient was stabilized, discharged home on oral pain medications, and advised to continue her birth control and follow up with her gynecologist.
